description: We’re creating an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Training game inspired by NASA missions and astronaut training. Players will complete space, science, problem-solving, and mission challenges. We’ll use AI to assist with coding, ideas, troubleshooting, and development. Team members can contribute through coding, research, game design, art, storytelling, or testing.
summary:
Lunar Frontier is an interactive lunar outpost management game designed to introduce students ages 7–12 to the engineering challenges of living and working on the Moon. Players take command of a simulated research base near the lunar South Pole, where they must balance life support, electrical power, and radiation protection while making decisions that affect their mission's success.

Through daily challenges, resource management, and unexpected events, players experience how one decision can affect several parts of an outpost. The game turns complex space exploration concepts into understandable, interactive lessons. It aims to make STEM education more engaging while helping young learners understand the planning, teamwork, and engineering required for sustainable human exploration of the Moon.
details:
Lunar Frontier is a mobile-friendly, browser-based lunar outpost management simulator.

Players take the role of an outpost commander responsible for keeping a lunar research base operational over a simulated 30-day mission. Each day presents decisions involving limited resources, including life support, electrical power, and radiation shielding. Different choices produce different consequences, teaching players that mission resources are connected and that no decision is completely free.

The project is designed for students ages 7–12, using simplified explanations, an interactive dashboard, mission events, and a scoring system to make space engineering easier to understand.

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with AI assistance from ChatGPT for code generation, game design, and written content. Development prioritizes mobile accessibility, straightforward gameplay, educational value, and replayability.

The intended impact is to help younger students understand the real engineering trade-offs involved in maintaining a human presence on the Moon, while encouraging curiosity about space exploration, science, and technology.

The game uses simplified simulation values for gameplay. These are distinguished from actual NASA measurements and scientific data.
